title: A Mechanistic Analysis of In-Context Learning and Out-of-Context Hallucination
abstract: arXiv:2611.24000v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models can infer and follow specific rules through in-context learning (ICL), yet may fail to remain faithful to provided evidence, giving rise to out-of-context (OOC) hallucination. Existing work has largely investigated the underlying mechanisms of ICL and OOC hallucination along separate lines. However, this separation obscures the mechanistic basis for these seemingly opposing outcomes. In this work, we study this contrast through the unified view of functional roles in dynamic context. The key observation is that role information can be internally represented without reliably constraining output. We derive a first-order decomposition to characterize the role effect, showing that its substantial influence depends on two necessary conditions, namely sufficient contribution magnitude and coherent signed aggregation. translated_title: 上下文学习与上下文外幻觉的机制分析
translated_abstract: 大语言模型能够通过上下文学习（ICL）推断并遵循特定规则，但却可能无法忠实于所提供的证据，从而产生上下文外（OOC）幻觉。现有工作大多沿着各自独立的路线分别研究ICL和OOC幻觉的内在机制。然而，这种割裂掩盖了这些看似对立的结果背后的机制基础。在这项工作中，我们通过动态上下文中功能角色的统一视角来研究这种对比。关键观察是，角色信息可以在模型内部被表示，但不一定能可靠地约束输出。我们推导了一阶分解来刻画角色效应，表明其显著影响取决于两个必要条件，即足够的贡献幅度和一致的带符号聚合。因果分析进一步表明，角色跨度的贡献会影响涉及响应的关键token选择。
tldr: 本文通过动态上下文中功能角色的统一视角，首次将上下文学习与上下文外幻觉这两种看似对立的现象联系起来进行机制分析，发现角色效应的显著影响取决于足够的贡献幅度和一致的带符号聚合这两个必要条件。
en_tdlr: This paper provides a unified mechanistic analysis of in-context learning and out-of-context hallucination through the lens of functional roles in dynamic context, showing that substantial role effects require two necessary conditions: sufficient contribution magnitude and coherent signed aggregation.
